MINUTES
  MALIBU CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING
  OCTOBER 9, 2023
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  6:30 P.M.

  The following meeting was held pursuant t0 AB 361 and teleconferenced from various
  locations during the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic.

  MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Uhring called the meeting to order at 5:30 pm.

  ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Steve Uhring; Mayor Pro Tem Doug Stewart; and Councilmembers
  Paul Grisanti, Marianne Riggins, and Bruce Silverstein

  PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION

  Mayor Uhring opened the floor to public comment.

MLJL. _L  Speakers: None.

  RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION

  At 5:02 p.m., the Council recessed to Closed Session to discuss the following item listed
  on the Closed Session agenda:

  Conference with Legal Counsel — Existing litigation pursuant to Government Code Section
  54956.9(d)(1):

  1.  Case Name: City’s Petition to Form Malibu USD from Territory in the Santa
  Monica-Malibu USD

  REGULAR SESSION CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Uhring called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m.

  ROLL CALL

  The followingpersons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Steve Uhring; Mayor Pro Tem Doug Stewart; and Councilmembers
  Paul Grisanti, Marianne Riggins, and Bruce Silverstein
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of October 9, 2023
  Page 2 of 16

  ALSO PRESENT: Trevor Rusin, Interim City Attorney; Steve McClary, City Manager;
  Joseph Toney, Assistant City Manager; Alexis Brown, Deputy City Manager; Kelsey
  Pettijohn, City Clerk; Kristin Riesgo, Community Services Director; Yolanda Bundy,
  Environmental Sustainability Director; Richard Mollica, Planning Director; Susan Dueflas,
  Public Safety Director; Rob DuBoux, Public Works Director; Christina Wood, Deputy City
  Attorney; Christina Munoz, Deputy City Clerk; Paolo Quinto, Environmental Health
  Administrator; Fletcher Allen, Assistant Planner; Raneika Brooks, Senior Planner; Tyler
  Eaton, Senior Planner; and Nadia Fahoum, Assistant Civil Engineer

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Don Schmitz led the Pledge of Allegiance.

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

  Interim City Attorney Rusin reported that the meeting convened at 5:30 p.m., after which
  time the City Council recessed to a Closed Session pursuant to Government Code Section
  54956.9(d)(l), with all Councilmembers present. He stated the Council discussed the'item
  listed on the closed session agenda and took no reportable action.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  City Clerk Pettijohn reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted on
  September 29, 2023, with the amended agenda posted on October 6, 2023.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Councilmember Silverstein moved, and Mayor Uhring seconded a motion to: l)
  approve the agenda; 2) adj ourn in support of the Victims in Israel and Palestine; 3)
  hear Item No. 3.B.4. concurrently with Item No. 5.A.; and 4) hear Item Nos. 6.A.
  after the Consent Calendar.

FRIENDLY AMENDMENT
  Councilmember Riggins moved to hear Item Nos. 5.A. and 6.B. after Item No. 6.A.

  The amendment was accepted by the maker and the seconder of the motion.

  The question was called, and the amended motion carried unanimously.

MOTION  Councilmember Silverstein moved, and Mayor Uhring seconded a motion to
  continue Item No. 4.B. to the October 23, 2023 Regular meeting. The question was
  called, and the motion failed 2-3, Councilmembers Grisanti and Riggins and Mayor
  Pro Tem Stewart opposed.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of October 9, 2023
  Page 3 of 16

  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  Presentation of City Tile to Fletcher Allen for Seven Years of Service to the City
  of Malibu

  Mayor Uhring presented a City Tile to Fletcher Allen, Assistant Planner, for seven
  years of service to the City of Malibu.

  Assistant Planner Allen thanked the Council for the recognition.

  Update Regarding Separation from Santa Monica-Malibu Unified School District

  Deputy City Attorney Wood presented the update regarding separation from Santa
  Monica-Malibu Unified School District.

  Presentation on Environmental Health Program Updates

  Environmental Sustainability Director Bundy and Environmental Health
  Administrator Quinto provided a presentation on Environmental Health Program
  updates.

ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Jill Hawkins discussed the importance of equal access to public education for
  unvaccinated individuals, vaccine status discrimination, and her concerns about
  vacc1nes.

  Maggie Rooney deferred time to Ms. Drummond.

  Ann Doneen deferred time to Ms. Drummond.

  Jo Drummond commended Environmental Health Administrator Quinto for his
  assistance on her project. She discussed the Ann Ravel letter and requested
  Councilmembers Grisanti and Riggins remove their Flaming Commissioner
  appointees, Dennis Robert Smith and Skylar Peak, in response to the letter. She
  discussed conflict of interest in the appointment of commissioners. She requested
  the matter be discussed at a public Special City Council meeting.

  Steven deferred time to Mr. Hassemi.

  David Hassemi discussed his house and trees his neighbor planted that obstructed
  his View of the city and ocean. He presented pictures of the View from his home
  and requested his View to be restored.

  Jefferson Wagner discussed the Ann Ravel letter and the California Fair Political
  Practices Commission (FPPC). He discussed transparency and previous searches of
  his property when he was on the Council. He stated that he knew both Planning
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of October 9, 2023
  Page 4 of 16

Commissioners referenced in the letter as respected members ofthe community but
stated that the letter merited some consideration. He discussed his recusal from
proj ects near his home when he served on the Council.
Kevin Shenkman discussed the Santa Monica California Voting Rights Act
litigation. He discussed trustee area elections for the Santa Monica-Malibu Unified
School District. He announced a rally would be held on October 10, 2023 at 5:00
pm. outside of Santa Monica City Hall to convince their City Council to stop the
expensive eight-year legal battle against voting rights.

Jake Lingo discussed coordination of field use at Bluffs Park by Malibu Little
League and the American Youth Soccer Organization (AYSO) and conflicts with
Maj or League Soccer’s youth program, MLS GO to the detriment of Little League
and AYSO. He discussed the work and equipment provided by AYSO to maintain
the fields. He requested that the City honor their decades-old tradition of hosting
community-based sports leagues at Bluffs Park and not sacrifice precious field
space for new organizations. He stated that he was working With City staff on
allocation of field space.

Tim Ryan deferred time to Scott Schoenberger.

Scott Schoenberger discussed AYSO and stated that he was with the 59-year-old
program for more than 20 years. He discussed the benefits of soccer on youth, the
volunteers extensive training for safety, and equipment maintenance. He thanked
the Council for their support.

Amor Magna discussed AYSO field space conflicts with MLS GO and read the
response letter that was submitted to the City.

Lloyd Ahern discussed an appropriation item on the upcoming Administration and
Finance Subcommittee meeting agenda. He discussed lighting issues in the Council
Chambers and asked the subcommittee to put a caveat on funding that allowed
additional funds to be made available for the proj ect. He stated that the background
for speakers at the podium needed to be changed to allow more visibility of
speakers. He discussed better camera coverage for Council meetings. ,

Paul Bellman discussed AYSO history as a nationwide non-profit organization and
their coordination with Malibu Little League.

John Alfano discussed Malibu Little League and thanked the City for their support
and improvements to Bluffs Park. He spoke in support of AYSO and the parent and
volunteer efforts and expense in field maintenance. He discussed field space
coordination challenges.

Howard Rudzki discussed City staffing issues and challenges in employee retention
which included inadequate staffing and excessive workload.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of October 9, 2023
  Page 5 of 16

  Ryan Embree discussed potential solutions to tied votes at the Planning
  Commission. He recommended the Council appoint one or two alternate Planning
  Commissioners as other cities had to avoid disruption in the City’s business.

  Matthew North discussed the important role of information in decision making.

  Bill Sampson discussed the FPPC matter and stated that the presumption of
  innocence was a criminal law concept. He stated that he did not believe there was
  wrongdoing by the Planning Commissioners referenced in the Ann Ravel letter but
  that there should be recusals when there was even the appearance of conflict of
  interest.

  Kraig Hill discussed permit review fees. He discussed conflict of interest in
  Flaming Commission decisions and the Ann Ravel letter and stated that if the
  claims had merit, they should be addressed. He clarified that he had not called for
  the resignation of the Commissioners in question. He stated that those called to
  testify as witnesses for the FPPC were not necessarily the complainants. He stated
  that the Commissioners in question should recuse themselves during the FPPC
  inquiry and spoke in favor of appointment of temporary alternate Commissioners.
  He clarified that he only voted to send the 6734 Zumirez appeal heard by the
  Flaming Commission to City Council because he was advised by the City Attorney
  that it was required.
  ”the
  Alicia Peak thanked  Councilmembers for their service and commended
  Community Services staff for their work. She discussed controversies over use of
  the pool and City playing fields. She recommended the organizations in
  disagreement communicate and cooperate for the sake ofthe community. She stated
  that the conflicts highlighted that a new pool and more field space was needed.

  Hovsep, Henry Himmel, Christopher Barry, Randy Fine, and Mary Phagan were
  not available at the time of the hearing.

ITEM 2.B.  COMMISSION / COMMITTEE / CITY MANAGER UPDATES

  City Manager McClary discussed the approval of Assembly Bill (AB) 1500 for the
  three-year extension of property tax exemptions for those affected by the 2018
  Woolsey Fire. He reported that Deputy City Manager Brown met with Los Angeles
  County Supervisor Lindsey Horvath the past week to discuss issues that impacted
  Malibu. He reported that he attended last week’s Environmental Sustainability
  Subcommittee meeting where Dark Sky Ordinance compliance was discussed. He
  announced there was an Administration and Finance Subcommittee meeting
  scheduled for October 10, 2023, at 10:00 a.m. where the Trancas Park restoration
  project and allocation of funds for Council Chambers lighting and broadcast
  improvements would be discussed. He stated that the City submitted comments to
  the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) on September 29, 2023, regarding their
  noise policy review and urged them to adopt rules that reduced noise caused by
  their Los Angeles International Airport aircraft route changes. He stated that a press
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of October 9, 2023
  Page 6 of 16

release on the City’s six-month goals was in progress. He éommended Public Safety
Director Dueflas for her flre preparation presentation at the prior week’s Business
Roundtable meeting. He announced the release of the request for proposals for the
community outreach consultant for the City’s vacant property uses. He announced'
the screening of the Halloween animated classic the Addams Family at Bluffs Park
would be held on Friday, October 13, 2023. He announced the Malibu Library
Speaker Series would be held on Wednesday, October 18, 2023, at 7:00 pm. at City
Hall featuring author David Quammen. He announced the Environmental
Sustainability Department would have an outreach booth at the October 15, 2023,
farmers’ market. He reported the Woolsey Fire rebuild statistics to date: 272
building permits for single-family homes were issued, 143 single-family dwellings
were complete, 18 multi—family building permits were issued, and 12 multi-family
building units were complete. He stated that a detailed report was forthcoming on
the analysis of the issuance of the special event permit (SEP) for the September 22,
2023 event on Via Linda Street, and provided an update on the preliminary
research. He provided statistics on SEP issuance since 2019 and stated there were
186 issued, with 10 of those submitted the day prior to the event.

Sergeant Soderlund, Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department, provided the
September 2023 crime statistics. He reported 352 part-one crimes year-to-date
which demonstrated a 9.5 percent reduction from the 389 at the same time in 2022.
He reported an individual was arrested on Pacific Coast Highway (PCH) for assault
and criminal threats. He reported an individual was arrested for theft and
trespassing on Sweetwater Canyon Drive. He reported an individual was arrested
for arson on PCH. He reported an individual was arrested for theft and vandalism
on Civic Center Way. He reported there were seven burglaries and one theft from
vehicles on PCH in the Malibu Lagoon and Surfrider Beach area. He reminded the
public to lock their vehicles and secure their valuables. He reported the recent
Malibu triathlon had no major issues. He provided an update on the incident that
involved the body found in a barrel the Malibu Lagoon and stated their Homicide
Bureau had made major progress in the case. He reported that there was a fatality
on Malibu Canyon ROad the night prior, where a driver hit a power pole at a high
rate of speed. He discussed the zero-bail policy that started on October 1, 2023, and
stated that only serious and Violent felony offenders would be jailed, with others
released onsite with a citation for a court appearance.

In response to Councilmember Silverstein, he stated that the assault, theft,
trespassing, and arson arrests were of unhoused individuals. He stated that he did
not have information on whether the body found in Malibu Lagoon was deceased
in Malibu. He stated that if an individual committed a crime while out on zero-bail,
whether they were taken into custody was dependent on the level of crime they
committed, and the same policy would be applied despite it being a second offense.

City Manager McClary stated that a discussion item on the zero-bail policy would
be on the next Regular Council meeting agenda.

In response to Councilmember Riggins, Sergeant Soderlund stated that Surfrider
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of October 9, 2023
  Page 7 of 16

‘J,
  Beach, as a State Beach had their own signage, but there was the electronic board
  \  on Malibu Canyon Road and signage in other areas that reminded people to lock
  their vehicles and secure their valuables.

  Councilmember Grisanti cautioned that vehicle doors could be opened without
  locating the key fob if it was-hidden on the vehicle. He stated that the Las Virgenes-
  Malibu Council of Governments (COG) had a meeting discussing the zero-bail
  policy.
  Mayor Urhing commented on racing on PCH on Friday and Saturday nights and
  stated that speed cameras would be helpful in reducing incidents of speeding.

  ITEM 2.C.  SUBCOMMITTEE REPORTS / COUNCIL COMMENTS

  Councilmember Silverstein thanked the public speakers and those who submitted
  written comments. He discussed the posted amended meeting agenda which
  removed the Closed Session item that addressed leasing at the Malibu Lumber
  Yard. He commented that Item No. 7.A. on the October 16, 2023 Flaming
  Commission meeting agenda was a staff presentation on Formula Retail Ordinance
  clearance with a single-page agenda report that was inadequate for the
  Commissioners, City Council, and the public for discussion preparation. He stated
  that a written presentation provided in advance of the meeting was required for a
  recommendation of receive and file. He stated that a written presentation would be
  helpiill when the Malibu Lumber Yard matter was brought back to the Council. He
  QJ4aL~V

  stated that he conducted his own analysis of the Formula Retail Ordinance
  application. He requested consensus on directing staff to table Item No. 7.A. on the
  October26, 2023 Planning Commission meeting agenda and place a Formula Retail
  Ordinance discussion item on the City Council agenda.

  The Council discussed the matter and directed questions to staff.

  CONSENSUS
  By consensus, the Council directed staff to bring back a report on Formula Retail
  Clearance.

  Councilmember Silverstein discussed the FPPC complaint from Ann Ravel
  regarding Skylar Peak and Dennis Smith’s participation on the Flaming
  Commission. He requested a Special meeting to discuss the complaint be scheduled
  for that week. He requested that Councilmembers Grisanti and Riggins recuse
  themselves prior to commencement of discussion on the matter as he had done
  during a previous unrelated matter.

  In response to Councilmember Silverstein, Interim City Attorney Rusin provided
  clarification on recusal criteria.

  Councilmember Grisanti thanked everyone who reminded them that it was election
  seaSOI’I.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of October 9, 2023
  Page 8 of 16

  Councilmember Riggins discussed the complaint to the FPPC and their pending
  investigation and stated that it was going to have far-reaching applications if it were
  determined to be factual that a licensed contractor could not sit on a commission of
  a city where they resided.

  Councilmember Silverstein commented on the Ann Ravel letter about conflict of
  interest. He provided a summary of discussions on the matter at previous Council
  and Flaming Commission meetings and a chronology of events which he found
  questionable. He stated his reasons for asking for consensus on holding a Special
  public meeting no later than Thursday of that week.

  Councilmember Grisanti explained the website Councilmember Silverstein
  referenced was outdated and from his time at Coldwell Banker. He stated that as a
  realtor, people sought his advice on projects, which was not atypical.

  Mayor Uhring stated that they had a responsibility to the residents to appear ethical
  and transparent and that it was a serious complaint that deserved a serious response
  from the City and should not be ignored.

  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart stated that the matter should be discussed in closed session
  as it was in alignment with Councilmember Silverstein’s assertion that the parties
  referenced in the letter should not speak publicly. He commented on the
  politicalization of the City Council and stated that they had worked well together
  for ten months. He thanked all parties involved in the triathlon and the money raised
  for the Children’s. Hospital. He indicated agreement with Ms. Peak’s comments
  about community needs for a pool and playing fields and that cooperation was
  needed between conflicting parties in the meantime. He commented on the Ann
  Ravel letter and stated that he was the only Councilmember who was not a
  respondent or a witness and speculated that attorney Ms. Ravel was retained by an
  unnamed client. He requested that perspective be kept on the matter as they await
  action by the FPPC.

  In response to Councilmember Silverstein, Interim City Attorney Rusin clarified
  the criteria for holding a closed session meeting.

  Councilmember Silverstein discussed the two appeals he submitted to the
  California Coastal Commission (CCC) and stated that the complaints he filed were
  on his oWn behalf and not that of a client, and that could be the case for the Ann
  Ravel letter. He stated that the City Council needed to take charge of the City’s
  response, and if it was not in alignment with Council direction, he would respond
  himself.

  Mayor Uhring stated that he did not know why he was called as a Witness on the
  matt6r.

CONSENSUS
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of October 9, 2023
  Page 9 of 16

  By consensus, the Council directed staff to schedule a Special meeting by
  Thursday, 0ctober 12, 2023, to hold a Closed SessiOn to discuss issues raised by
  the allegations in the FPPC complaint submitted by Ann Ravel.

  Councilmember Grisanti reported that he recently had a conversation with
  Supervisor Horvath about a grant for remediation of beaches in Los Angeles
  County, half of which would benefit Malibu. He reported that he attended part of
  the Business Roundtable meeting.

  Councilmember Riggins thanked the public speakers who commented on the field
  space shortage and commended the AYSO and Little League for their years ofwork
  in the community. She suggested groups new to Malibu research facilities, rules,
  and requirements and contact City staff at least three months in advance of the
  beginning of their planned activity. She thanked Assemblymember Jacqui Irwin
  and her team, City staff, and those who helped get AB 1500 passed. She stated that
  she attended the Environmental Sustainability Subcommittee meeting, and they
  reviewed Dark Sky Ordinance compliance. She encouraged residents to learn the
  requirements of the ordinance as it would be applied to residential properties soon.
  She announced that the Environmental Review Board would be hearing the skate
  park project proposal on Wednesday, October 11, 2023. She encouraged the public
  to get involved in the process of exploring the use of the City’s vacant land. In
  response to Mr. Hassemi, she encouraged him to work with staff on view protection
  and the process in place.

  Mayor Uhring thanked the public speakers. He encouraged AYSO and Little
  League to work with Community Services Director Riesg'o about field space
  challenges. In response to Mr. Rudzki, he stated that he agreed that staff was
  overworked which was why they limited the strategic priority project list to 20 at
  the recent Special City Council meeting. He discussed the community’s perception
  of ethics, transparency, and fair treatment in favor ofthe rich and famous, and stated
  there were numerous actions by the City that support their concern. He discussed
  the Whole Foods shopping center that was based on a traffic study that indicated
  Malibu traffic had not increased in 25 years and the open space requirement being
  met by the construction of walls covered in foliage. He discussed recent special
  events and the lease arrangement at the Malibu Lumber Yard. He discussed the
  FPPC complaint and suggested cooperation and appropriate action be taken by the
  City.

ITEM 3  CONSENT CALENDAR

MOTION  Councilmember Riggins moved, and Councilmember Silverstein seconded a
  motion to approve the Consent Calendar, pulling Item No. 3.B.4 to be heard
  concurrently with Item No. 5.A. The question was called, and the motion carried
  unanimously.

ITEM 6  NEW BUSINESS

  Recommended Action: 1) Receive a presentation on outdoorwarning sirens; and
  2) Provide direction to staff regarding the implementation of an outdoor warning
  system.

  Public Works Director DuBoux presented the staff report.

  The Council directed questions to staff.

  Mayor Uhring opened the floor to public comment.

  Speakers: John Mazza, Jo Drummond, and Ryan Embree

  As there were no other speakers present, Mayor Uhring returned the matter to the
  table for discussion.

MOTION  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart moved, and Mayor Uhring seconded a motion to direct
  staff to pursue Alternative 4 — Indoor Notification Systems identified in the staff
  report. The question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

MOTION  Councilmember Riggins moved, and Councilmember Silverstein seconded a
  motion to continue Item No. 4.B. to the October 23, 2023 Regular City Council
